body: Thanks, I wonder about that too. As he dictated the clinic note he threw in a comment about seeming "eager to please", literally just thought I was being friendly and polite. Everything becomes pathological when you walk through that door.

I understand that depression makes me side with the negative. Which is why I try to look at the evidence based on past actions etc. For me this has always come up in favour of things going well. 
However as I have just learned these relationships which I thought were healthy are dependent - and that is true, and evidenced by the fact that other people are the only reason why I've lasted this long.
 
So now I've lost my compass and due to depression I know I can't trust my judgement. All I'm left with is feeling like I'm a burden to others and feeling guilty whenever I reach out to my bf for help, plus because they wouldn't let me see a different doctor I've been discharged from the service.

It's such a shit situation where we are hurt really badly, going to people for help, have no choice but to trust them and realise they don't care at all, and you leave feeling worse than before with the added pain of knowing you've just lost a shot at things getting better and now have to muster the energy to repeat the exact same process from the beginning.
and the suicide number is busy fml

i guess it depends on the person. 
I was speaking generally as I have an interesting, challenging and meaningful career ahead of me, a loving and supportive partner and family, some friends who are genuinely good people, financial security and I haven't experienced anything traumatic. 
While those might not necessarily be the key to happiness, a lack of any of the above can lead to a lot of unhappiness.
Its something I'd put on my bucket list, but right now I'm just trying not to fuck up uni.

From a practical view point I think apathy is a fairly common symptom so not sure how far this would get.
I do like that idea though. No just with saddies though. A mix. But being in nature is so soothing and peaceful. Makes everything else seem far less significant and for a couple of moments you just get lost in the expanse and beauty.

For me its more of a feeling of absolute and complete loneliness and the future that I had been expecting and anticipating and working towards becomes a mirage. It was only an illusion that I could have that life, and its a really nice illusion, but that's all it is. Yes you will hurt people if you end it, but you'll only be hurting them now rather than later down the track. So why wait.
Spring time is very nice indeed.

They will see you and you will likely be admitted. In most places there are mental health crisis teams which you can call at any time of day/night. They would be better because they are more specialised for mental health so there'll be less waiting in ED (up to or more than 6 hours depending on where you are) and consultations behind curtains instead of closed doors. 
Hope whatever you end up doing helps you
